title: notice.show
description: host → server → client (relayed unchanged). The host shows a short text on phones: CAPCOM subtitle, hint, "what just happened" summary, classroom discussion prompt, fact moment or warning. Text is always a string-table reference.

text.description: Text to show (≤ 25 words on screen, §12.1).

factId.description: Fact shown (kind FACT), so the phone can link to the Codex; null otherwise.

durationMs.description: How long to show it; 0 = until dismissed by the user.

to.description: Players to show it to; null = every player and spectator.

DataId.description: Identifier of an entry in the shared game data (`data/`): part, part category, contract, test, anomaly card, minigame, fact, codex entry, callout, console request, award, objective, validation rule, cosmetic. 1–48 characters.

NoticeKind.description: Kind of host notice shown on phones.

PlayerId.description: Player identifier, unique within a room and never reused: "p" followed by a positive integer (p1, p2, …).

TextRef.description: Reference to localised player-visible text. The protocol never carries free display text: `key` is a key of `data/strings/<lang>.json`, and `args` supplies substitution values. Receivers format numbers and units locally.

args.description: Substitution values by placeholder name. String values must themselves be data ids or string-table keys, never user text.
